So a chain of slow services: ts-train-service appears to be the innermost slow own-work, with basic/travel/travel2/route-plan/travel-plan/preserve all waiting on it (basic->train, travel->basic->train, route-plan->travel->basic->train). Hypothesis: ts-train-service (or its pods) is the origin. Next: check pod-level resource metrics (CPU, memory, GC, threads) for ts-train-service and ts-basic-service in abnormal vs normal, and inspect the train service's leaf span durations.

## Root-cause findings

**Bottom line:** One root cause. `ts-train-service` adds a fixed ~3.6 s delay to every call on its train-lookup endpoints. The delay sits in the controller code, not in the database. Latency propagates upstream through `ts-basic-service`, then into travel, travel2, route-plan, travel-plan and preserve. No errors were introduced; this is purely a latency degradation.

### Root cause (single origin)

**ts-train-service, pod `ts-train-service-9b56d75b6-jm6nj`**
- `POST /api/v1/trainservice/trains/byNames`: min 3594 ms, p50 3595 ms. Every call pays roughly the same ~3.6 s floor. Normal p50 is in the low single-digit ms range.
- `TrainController.retrieveByName`: about 3594 ms average (range 3593–3612 ms). This is also used by `GET /trains/byName/{name}` (p50 ~3595 ms, min 2.8 ms, so some calls are fast).
- Its DB child spans are fast: `TrainTypeRepository.findByNames` averages 2.4 ms and `findByName` 3.4 ms. The roughly 3.59 s gap sits between the controller and its DB work, which points to injected wait or blocking code in the controller path rather than to MySQL.
- Resource metrics do not explain it. CPU time, memory, JVM class/buffer counts and DB connection pool (max 10, pending 0) look like normal. JVM CPU time is lower than in normal runs, which argues against CPU-bound work.
- Logs from this service show only INFO lines and do not name the cause.

### Propagation path (affected endpoints)

| Service (endpoint) | Normal avg | Abnormal avg | Driven by |
|---|---|---|---|
| ts-basic-service (`queryForTravel(s)`, `POST /basic/travel(s)`) | ~21 ms | ~1.8 s (3.6 s on affected calls) | ts-train `byNames` |
| ts-travel-service (`trips/left`, `trip_detail`) | ~33 ms | ~0.7 s (3.7 s on affected calls) | ts-basic |
| ts-travel2-service (`trips/left`, `trip_detail`) | ~36 ms | ~0.9 s (3.7 s on affected calls) | ts-basic |
| ts-route-plan-service (`cheapestRoute`, `quickestRoute`, `minStopStations`) | ~181 ms | ~3.3 s (7.4–8.6 s on affected calls) | ts-travel / ts-travel2 |
| ts-travel-plan-service (`cheapest`, `quickest`, `minStation`) | ~188 ms | ~4.8 s (15–17 s on affected calls) | ts-route-plan / ts-train |
| ts-preserve-service (`preserve`) | ~107 ms | ~2.7 s (7.5 s on affected calls) | ts-basic / ts-travel |

The user-facing `ts-ui-dashboard` latency rose from ~62 ms to ~800 ms average (p95 ~3.7 s). That is the symptom the support ticket describes.

### Unaffected services (ruled out)
- `ts-route-service` (~3 ms), `ts-seat-service`, `ts-order-service`, `ts-auth-service`, `ts-config-service`, `ts-price-service`, `ts-station-service`, `ts-user-service`, `ts-verification-code-service`: latency is unchanged from normal.
- No new error status codes appear in any service. The existing ERROR/WARN log lines (`ts-food-service`, `ts-order-other-service`, the auto-delete queue errors in notification and delivery) are also present in the normal baseline and do not change.

### Number of faults
The evidence supports **one** root-cause fault. Every slow chain traces back to the ~3.6 s floor in ts-train-service. I did not find a second independent origin.
